hypotheses.description: First-valid-wins proof races collapse to a unique fastest entrant in the deterministic speed-ranking model.
hypotheses.key_finding: With reward 10, the fastest prover at cost 7 enters and earns 3; slower provers with costs 5 and 1 lose for sure if they enter and therefore prefer exit. If the globally fastest prover is not profitable, the next-fastest profitable prover becomes the unique entrant.

hypotheses.description: The halving proof-mining reward schedule creates a participation cliff before a pre-funded pool is exhausted.
hypotheses.key_finding: At base reward 64 and prover cost 9, epochs 0..2 pay enough to participate, epoch 3 pays 8 and participation stops, leaving 888 of a 1000 pool. The bounded grid matches E_stop = min(epoch_cap + 1, bit_length(base // cost)) for cost > 1; cost-one provers remain active because the implemented schedule floors rewards at one.

hypotheses.description: Permissionless-hosting improvement ties are selectable because `_route_tiebreak_key` includes submitter-chosen `miner_id` and route shape.
hypotheses.key_finding: For equal routes and equal improvements, miner_id '0000' sorts before 'zzzz' and wins the tie under the implemented key order; one-hop routes also sort before two-hop routes for the same miner_id.

hypotheses.description: Per-round bounty caps and per-round base rewards make improvement withholding profitable in a concrete integer witness.
hypotheses.key_finding: With base_reward 10, improvement_reward_bps 2500, max_reward 25, and δ = 80, one-shot payout is capped at 25 while two δ/2 submissions pay 20 + 20 = 40 across rounds.

hypotheses.description: The exact sybil submission-fee floor for flooding S slots is ceil(reward / S).
hypotheses.key_finding: For rewards 1..128 and caps 1..16, flooding payoff reward - S * fee is non-positive exactly when fee >= ceil(reward / S), and one unit below the threshold is profitable when the threshold exceeds one.

hypotheses.description: Proof-mining pool conservation holds under admissible-award semantics with rejected claims treated as no-ops.
hypotheses.key_finding: Across a mixed valid/invalid epoch sequence, every admissible claim updates total_paid and pool so total_paid + pool remains the initial pool; invalid claims and insufficient-budget claims are modeled as no-ops.
